issues.title: Unicode characters in print() without encoding guard
issues.description: Print statements use Unicode characters (U+2713 ✓, U+2717 ✗) that cannot be encoded by the Windows cp1252 console codec. This caused UnicodeEncodeError on all 3 Windows CI jobs (Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12), failing before any determinism test could execute.
issues.root_cause: Python stdout defaults to the system locale encoding on Windows (cp1252). Unicode chars outside the ASCII range fail unless PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 is set or a fallback is provided.
issues.resolution: Added PYTHONIOENCODING: utf-8 to the CI workflow environment in .github/workflows/pr26-cross-platform.yml so all Python versions on all platforms use UTF-8 for stdout.
issues.falsification_test: Run 'python tests/test_pr26_cross_machine.py' on Windows without PYTHONIOENCODING set — should raise UnicodeEncodeError at line 312.

issues.title: Integer projection weight update rule not implemented (FUTURE WORK)
issues.description: The train_step() method in runtime.py performs a forward pass but does not apply weight updates. The docstring explicitly labels this 'a simplified placeholder implementation' and the integer projection update rule (Delta_W = (E @ Input.T) mod 2^64) is marked as FUTURE WORK. As a result, no learning occurs and the convergence claim cannot be falsified by the existing test suite.
issues.root_cause: Sequential integer backpropagation requires a non-standard autograd mechanism. The current implementation defers this work.
issues.resolution: Claim is explicitly documented in docstrings and PR description. The determinism claim (identical hash across machines) remains fully falsifiable and is the primary PR #26 invariant.
issues.falsification_test: Run train_step() and verify weights are unchanged before and after.

issues.title: Hard little-endian requirement excludes big-endian platforms
issues.description: CrossMachineGuarantee.enforce_deterministic_environment() raises RuntimeError on big-endian systems. The falsification test test_falsification_platform_specific_code() similarly asserts sys.byteorder == 'little'. This is correct for x86/ARM (all current CI runners are little-endian), but creates an undocumented platform boundary.
issues.root_cause: SHA256 byte expansion uses byteorder='little' in deterministic_expand(), so big-endian systems would produce different int64 bit patterns.
issues.resolution: The constraint is intentional and documented. All CI runners (Ubuntu/macOS/Windows on x86-64 and ARM64) are little-endian. A note could be added to README.
issues.falsification_test: Run on a SPARC or IBM Z system — should raise RuntimeError.

issues.title: GITHUB_OUTPUT write: newline='\n' in f-string (no extra \r on Windows)
issues.description:
The Capture model hash step writes hash=<value>
 to GITHUB_OUTPUT using Python's open() in append mode. On Windows, opening a file in text mode (default) translates 
 to 
. The f-string already embeds 
, so the file receives 
, which GitHub Actions correctly handles (it strips trailing whitespace). Status: Uses open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') with explicit newline in the f-string. Correct and safe.
issues.root_cause: Text-mode file write on Windows adds carriage return.
issues.resolution: Acceptable as-is since GitHub Actions strips trailing whitespace from GITHUB_OUTPUT values. No action needed.
issues.falsification_test: Read the GITHUB_OUTPUT file bytes on Windows and check for \r\n.

issues.title: update_weights_sequential() defined but never called
issues.description: runtime.py defines update_weights_sequential() which computes the integer projection weight delta but is not invoked anywhere. The method is present solely as a specification of the intended algorithm. This creates dead code that could mislead readers into thinking weight updates are active.
issues.root_cause: The training loop (train_step) intentionally skips the update because full sequential backpropagation is not yet implemented.
issues.resolution: Method is clearly documented as a placeholder. Acceptable given the explicit FUTURE WORK annotation.
issues.falsification_test: Grep for callers of update_weights_sequential — should find zero.

issues.title: safetensors int64 support version dependency
issues.description: runtime.py uses safetensors.torch.save_file/load_file for int64 tensors. safetensors added int64 support in version 0.3.0 (2023). requirements.txt already pins safetensors>=0.4.0 — constraint satisfied.
issues.root_cause: Potential missing minimum version constraint for safetensors.
issues.falsification_test: Install safetensors<0.3.0 and attempt save_file with int64 tensor.
